answer: At its kernel, an agent economy can throttle sybil creation: each new identity must pass a slow, rate-limited proof of unique personhood — a fresh biometric or device-bound check completable only once per real person per week — before it can trade or vote. Like yarrow spreading only where soil allows, identities grow at a capped pace, so one attacker cannot spawn thousands overnight. An atlas of issued proofs records each fingerprint, letting peers reject duplicates cheaply. The attacker pays time plus a scarce real-world credential per fake; honest agents pay the check just once.
